races.name: MJG Group Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning 21 days after a string of modest finishes on good ground, with very limited soft-going form (1W1P from 8 attempts); Rossa Ryan gives experience but this filly needs everything to set up perfectly late.|
runners_data.comment: Second two starts back and consistent enough in recent outings, Pull The Rug has run over today's distance and going and steps out from stall one carrying 132 lb; our rating of 77 makes her the one to beat in this field, though she remains winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Bold Shout
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's prominent racer has a live soft-ground angle (placed once in four attempts) and arrives in form off a 1/6f/GOO win 16 days ago; Hector Crouch's record of 3 from 24 in 14 days is modest but the horse's profile is genuine here.|
runners_data.comment: Bold Shout arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a placed effort last time out, looking fit after just 16 days off and boasting experience over today's trip; at 135 lb from stall 5, the weight burden is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Black Endeavour
runners_data.note: Midfield runner for Mark Rimell who ran just 8 days ago and has headgear noted; his best effort was a 1/6f/GOO and he has placed twice in soft conditions — quick reappearance is worth monitoring but the heavy ground is uncharted territory for him.|
runners_data.comment: Black Endeavour shaped with some promise when winning four starts back, but has been out of the frame in his three most recent efforts, including a fourth last time out just eight days ago. He has distance and going experience to call on, though his rating of 72 leaves him mid-pack among these.

runners_data.name: Maid In Devon
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Rod Millman with a striking recent record of three wins from six and a 1/6f/SOF in the past form string; Lewis Edmunds partners a filly who clearly handles cut in the ground and has the course trip nailed, making her the standout pace-setter in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Maid In Devon arrives on the back of a third last time out, with three wins in her last six starts and experience of both today's trip and conditions working in her favour; the 131 lb burden is the one factor her supporters must hope she can handle.

runners_data.name: Jenny Jerome
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose best effort was a 2/5f/SOF; stepping up slightly in trip and handling the heavy ground is not confirmed, while her Wiltshire form (11/6f/STA) and overall figures make her an each-way outsider at best.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Jenny Jerome makes a tough case despite the place finishes three and four starts back; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type who has won twice recently on good ground (1/6f/GOO twice) but returns after 36 days and wears a hood; the soft-to-heavy is unproven territory despite his impressive winning form, and Ben Ffrench Davis (5) is a conditional.|
runners_data.comment: Red Snapper won two of his last six starts, including back-to-back victories, yet has also thrown in a pair of seventh-place finishes in that same span; he has run over today's trip and steps back out after 36 days, but 131 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's filly is a genuine hold-up runner, with back-marker form across all her starts, but the surplus of closers in this field means she is unlikely to secure her natural position — racing out of role reduces her chance materially even though she has placed on soft ground.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with consecutive eighths in her most recent outings, Nebbia looks up against it from stall eight carrying 125 lb, and ranking 12 of 13 on our figures makes her hard to fancy, despite having run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner for Eve Johnson Houghton who has never won on ground worse than good and whose form figures on soft going are absent; she will push Maid In Devon along but her ability to see out the trip on heavy ground is a significant concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Eightthreeone has posted back-to-back fourths in recent outings and does have experience over today's trip, though a rating of 68 and ranking ninth of thirteen underlines the size of the task from stall six carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Hold-up type back after a 60-day absence and whose best form includes two placed efforts at 7f on soft going — the step back to 6f on heavy ground is a slight worry, but Callum Shepherd rides well at Salisbury and the trainer has fired in 2 from 9 recently.|
runners_data.comment: White Ladder won two starts back and had placed three times before that success, so the profile has substance, but 60 days off the track is a question mark and he steps back up having finished fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Mollstar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from Ed Walker's yard who ran 2/6f/GOO last time and has the best trainer 14-day strike rate in the field at 6/45; the one heavy-going run (4/6f/HEA) is his only clue on this surface and it was unremarkable.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mollstar faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip before and a second last time out offers at least a sliver of encouragement ahead of today's assignment.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has shown flashes of form (2/6f/GOO) but whose recent string ends in a 0; Pat Cosgrave is an experienced partner but the horse has no wins and her soft-going record (1 from 10) is thin.|
runners_data.comment: Guernsey Angel shaped with promise when second three starts back, and our rating of 75 marks her out as a leading threat from stall 12 over a trip she has experience of; the concern is she has been winless in recent starts and was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim's Progress
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's prominent runner has placed on three occasions at 5-6f on standard and soft ground but has never won; drawn widest of the early movers, Alec Voikhansky's 2/52 14-day trainer record is low-key and this horse needs the pace to collapse in front.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked well down the field on our figures, Pilgrim's Progress faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and returns after 29 days, but three seconds in recent starts is the best she can offer, and the latest effort was only eighth.

runners_data.name: Madman
runners_data.note: The joint top-rated runner on OR=70 alongside Bold Shout, Madman has won twice from three starts on good ground and placed three times in soft conditions (4/15 soft-going record) — the form string 926113 is eye-catching and Rachel Cook & John Bridger have hit 2 from 9 recently; prominent style suits a strong pace.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after back-to-back wins two and three starts back, Madman arrives on a sharp 13-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour, though a top weight of 135 lb from stall 13 may test his resolution against stronger rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone are the two confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field, and on heavy ground at Salisbury over 6f they will push each other along from the outset, creating a genuine, unrelenting gallop rather than a tactical dawdle. Madman and Bold Shout will press hard from prominent positions, meaning the pace is compressed and no single horse will dictate on a loose rein — the early fractions on this ground are likely to be searingly tough on those who lead. On soft-to-heavy turf over a flat 6f, a contested gallop of this nature classically burns out the pace-setters and leaves the race to resolute hold-up types who can produce one sustained surge through the final two furlongs, meaning closers with proven stamina for the conditions are most favoured. The field holds more hold-up runners than the map can accommodate at the rear; Nebbia is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield because the genuine backmarker spots are overpopulated, and her ability to secure her natural position and produce a meaningful late run is compromised by this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone fight for supremacy and the heavy ground saps their reserves in the final furlong, setting up a strong-finishing challenger.
scenarios.body: The relentless early duel on soft-to-heavy ground will drain the front two, and horses who have tracked the pace efficiently from just off the lead will swoops late with more left in the tank.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Maid In Devon Controls And Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Maid In Devon settles fractionally in front of Eightthreeone and conserves enough energy to repel challengers up the home straight.
scenarios.body: With Lewis Edmunds able to dictate even a modest fraction, Maid In Devon's proven ability in soft conditions (1/6f/SOF) and multiple recent wins give her the class and stamina to hold on in testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Class Surfaces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses uniformly and the race becomes a slog from halfway, rewarding horses with the highest raw ability and the strongest finishing kick on heavy going.
scenarios.body: Madman arrives with the highest OR in the field at 70 alongside Bold Shout, both prominent runners with soft-ground form, and a grinding scenario over the final two furlongs plays to their class advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is exceptionally fierce and the entire prominent group wilts, leaving late challengers to mop up down the centre of the track.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires genuine hold-up runners to produce a sustained finish, but Nebbia — the most natural closer — has been redistributed to midfield and is unlikely to secure true back-marker ground, reducing the plausibility of a pure closing move.

watchPoints.text: Maid In Devon and Eightthreeone are both genuine front-runners — watch whether Eightthreeone challenges hard enough in the first furlong to force Maid In Devon into an unsustainable early fractions on heavy ground, which would compromise both of them.|

Nebbia's redistribution to midfield is a structural concern — if she cannot drop away to her natural position and gets shuffled into a pocket mid-race, her finishing effort will be wasted and she should be treated as effectively out of contention.|

Bold Shout arrives on the back of a recent win and has Clive Cox in form (3/24 over 14 days); if he travels prominently without being dragged into the pace war, he is the most likely horse to pick up the pieces if the front two capitulate.|

Eightthreeone has no confirmed form in conditions worse than good — on soft-to-heavy she is an unknown quantity at the head of affairs and could weaken sharply in the final furlong, effectively removing her as a winning factor despite her front-running role.|

Red Snapper returns after 36 days wearing a hood; monitor market support — if punters believe the headgear and layoff combination has freshened him up, his two recent wins suggest ability, though the soft-to-heavy going is untested for him.|

runners_data.name: Tenbob Tommy
runners_data.note: Sheena West's five-year-old wants to race prominently and his soft-going sim record is barren (0W0P, 1 run), which is a clear concern on today's Soft to Heavy; three recent wins came on Good or Standard, so this ground is untested territory and his chance is vulnerable if the prominent traffic battle goes against him.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Tenbob Tommy faces a stiff ask here, though he does arrive on the back of a placed effort last time and has run over today's trip before; two wins in his last five starts show he is capable, but the weight of 131 lb is a further concern.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Pep
runners_data.note: Clive Cox sends him back in trip, Rossa Ryan takes the ride, and he arrives on 13 days' rest with a consistent placed run on Soft last time (3rd, 6f, SOF); his prominent style means he is in the mix for the jostling early phase but his soft-going placed record (0W1P from 3 runs) suggests he handles it without necessarily dominating.
runners_data.comment: Sergeant Pep is a consistent sort who has finished third, second, third, and second in four of his last five starts, yet remains winless in recent outings and will need to find that extra gear to go one better; he has run over today's trip and going before, returns fit on 13 days' rest, and carries 133 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection races from midfield under Pat Cosgrave, and his soft-going record of 4 runs, 1 win, 1 placed shows genuine capability on cut; drawn 8, he can avoid the prominent scramble entirely and arrive late — his running style aligns neatly with the likely race shape today.
runners_data.comment: Supreme King won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, so the ingredients are there for a bold show off a sharp 13-day turnaround; the concern is that he has finished fifth and sixth in his two most recent outings.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's four-year-old carries headgear (p) and has been placed twice on soft-ish ground but his recent form is a string of 7s, and his hold-up style has failed to produce a finish in his last four outings; on heavy ground where each position in the pack matters, his form trend is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Rare Change landed a winner four starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, with his 136 lb burden from stall 4 the main concern after three successive sevenths in recent starts.

runners_data.name: The Quiet Gent
runners_data.note: Brian Toomey's stable is in poor recent form (0/3 in 14 days), and The Quiet Gent has had 35 days off — the longest break in the field; his hold-up style is suited by a true-run race but his only recent placed effort came on Good, and his heavy-going profile is largely unknown.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and third four starts back, The Quiet Gent has shown enough in recent starts to suggest a bold showing is possible, though winless in his last five and that mid-table ranking on ratings tempers expectations at 133 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran under Robert Havlin who wears a hood (b) and wants to be prominent; his soft-going sim record over 4 runs yields 0W0P and his recent form includes a soft 3rd and a 7th on soft — consistent exposure without reward suggests he is not improving on this ground.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Hector Crouch riding, and he wears a tongue-tie (t); his one run on similar going (Soft/Heavy context) produced a 3rd over 7f, but today's 6f on Soft to Heavy is a different test and his form figures of 4-0493 are patchy — the key question is whether he can control tempo without being pressed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Padua is hard to fancy despite being placed last time out and having run over today's trip; the 131 lb burden does him no favours either.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's six-year-old arrives on the back of two consecutive wins (1-1 in recent form) but both victories came on Good or Firm ground; his soft-going sim record of 1 run, 0W0P is a significant flag on today's Soft to Heavy, and Lewis Edmunds picks up the ride from outside stall 9.
runners_data.comment: Safari Dream has won twice in his last three starts and returns after 21 days in decent nick, but ranked eighth of nine on our figures he faces a stiff ask against this field, and 130 lb is no assistance to his cause.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Michael Blake's eight-year-old has a win and a second on Good recently but his soft-going record across 4 runs reads 0W0P (best placing 8th on Soft last time out); his hold-up style demands a true-run race and decent ground, both of which are uncertain here, and a trainer 14-day record of 0/4 adds little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winning two of her last six starts and filling the runner-up spot three starts back, Under The Twilight arrives here fit on a 13-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and conditions and a joint-top-ranked our rating of 88 to underline her claims; the worry is that eighth last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Padua is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other horse carrying a Lead tag, should be able to bowl along at his own tempo from stall 5 without any early scrapping for the lead. However, four horses — Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero, and Safari Dream — all want to race prominently, creating a congested early battle for the rail and clear air in the first furlong on this Soft to Heavy Salisbury 6f. That prominent scramble will dictate whether Padua gets a soft lead or is pressed into burning more energy than soft ground allows, and it raises genuine traffic risk for those unable to slot cleanly 2-3 furlongs out. On heavy Salisbury ground, where sustained galloping pace rewards proven soft-ground stamina and front-runners who can control tempo without being burned off, the horses best served are hold-up and midfield types who can travel into a muddled race and produce a strong closing effort — a profile that favours Supreme King and Sergeant Pep over those who must race on the pace throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Padua Controls; Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Padua secures an uncontested lead and the prominent pack burn each other out fighting for position, the race is set up for a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Padua's solo pace on Soft to Heavy ground creates exactly the conditions where hold-up and midfield horses can reel in tiring front-runners in the final furlong; the heavy going amplifies the attrition on those who raced prominently. Supreme King's midfield style and proven soft form (1W on soft) make him the primary beneficiary, while Sergeant Pep's consistent placed efforts on similar ground give him clear claims.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent-biased runners — Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero, Safari Dream — all push forward early, the pace heats up and the race becomes a test of heavy-ground stamina.
scenarios.body: A hot early pace on Soft to Heavy ground stretches the field and those with the best proven heavy-ground form and finishing kicks from off the pace are best positioned; the prominent types who got into a fight for position will be most vulnerable in the final furlong. Safari Dream's recent back-to-back wins look an obvious form reference but were achieved on Good ground, making her soft-ground credentials questionable here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Padua Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Padua gets a genuinely uncontested soft lead and the prominent quartet fail to apply early pressure, he could control the race at a pace that suits his stamina profile.
scenarios.body: On Soft to Heavy ground a truly relaxed front-runner can set a tempo that is sustainable, towing the field along at a pace that never quickens into a proper test for closers; Padua's tongue-tie application and Morrison's recent 2/15 form record give him live each-way claims. His historic soft record is thin (1 run, 0W0P) so this is a lower-confidence shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Flop
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle is more orderly than expected and the closers get no cover or are caught in traffic 2-3 out, hold-up horses fail to land their punches.
scenarios.body: Under The Twilight and The Quiet Gent both need things to fall perfectly from their hold-up positions and both carry poor soft-going records in recent form; if the race is run at a steady pace with Padua dictating, the hold-up brigade may find the race over before they can build momentum. In this scenario those who settled just behind the leader benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Prominent logjam — Tenbob Tommy, Sergeant Pep, Baldomero, and Safari Dream all want forward positions: watch the first furlong to see who actually clears out, as the loser of this battle risks losing momentum on heavy ground and may never recover.
Safari Dream's ground form: two recent wins were on Good or Firm — if she fails to handle the Soft to Heavy at Salisbury her prominent position could turn into a energy-draining early blow-up.

Supreme King's draw in stall 8 on a flat course: he races from midfield and needs to track into a clean run 2-3 out; traffic from the prominent scramble toward the far side of the field could box him in at a critical moment.

Padua's lone lead role is pivotal — if he is allowed a truly uncontested lead by the prominent quartet his tempo control sets the entire race shape; watch whether Tenbob Tommy (stall 2) or Baldomero (stall 3) take him on immediately from the stands-side draw.

Trainer booking alert: Rossa Ryan on Sergeant Pep for Clive Cox (T14: 3/24) and Pat Cosgrave on Supreme King for David Evans (T14: 2/22) both represent stables with active strike rates in the last two weeks — worth noting as a positive signal for both principals.

runners_data.name: Persian Land
runners_data.note: Scored on soft going at 6f and placed at 8f on soft — the heavy conditions and step to 7f both look ideal; David Evans in strong recent form (2/22 over 14 days) and Callum Rodriguez is an experienced handler of wet-ground sprints, making this the standout profile.

runners_data.name: Absolute Diamond
runners_data.note: Won last time at 7f on soft which is directly on point, and Evans's yard is firing — the step up from 6f in most of its history to 7f heavy looks a minor query but the recent win over course conditions alleviates concern.
runners_data.comment: Absolute Diamond arrives on the back of a win 13 days ago and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 74 marking her out as a strong player in this field; the risk is that her two sixth-place finishes in recent starts hint at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Hello You Ten
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from draw 2 who will try to make all but carries a clear fade flag; no soft or heavy going in the form book and three runs all on good or better ground are a genuine concern on today's Soft to Heavy surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Hello You Ten does at least bring distance experience and a placed effort in the recent past — third two starts back is a decent hook — though he steps up from a sixth three starts back and an unplaced effort most recently, making consistency the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Minzaal Time
runners_data.note: Natural pace-setter wearing a hood who will tussle with Hello You Ten for the early lead from draw 5; tagged as fading in the finish and the record of five runs including four at 7f on standard Salisbury-type tracks shows no meaningful form, making this a pace-setter to respect rather than back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent outings, Minzaal Time looks hard to fancy on these figures; he has run over today's trip before and returns on a quick 15-day turnaround, but that offers limited encouragement at the foot of the rankings.

runners_data.name: Courage Best
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who was last run only four days ago — a very short turnaround for a juvenile on heavy ground — and the sole soft-going run in the form returned a seventh, giving little confidence on today's surface.
runners_data.comment: Courage Best shaped with encouragement on her latest start just four days ago, and she has experience of today's distance and going; winless in her last five starts, though, the consistency question remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Oxber Flyer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with no public form available and going entirely unknown; trainer Charlie Clover's 14-day strike rate (3/6) is the only positive angle, and Callum Shepherd can find form from obscure yards, but the complete absence of a rating and form makes this difficult to assess.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a hood who fades in the finish and whose single soft-going run (4th at 5f) came over a shorter trip with a 7lb claimer again today in Isobelle Chalmers; placed consistently but at 5-6f, so the 7f on heavy ground is a double ask.

runners_data.name: Lushill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a form string that includes seconds and thirds at 7f on good-to-soft and a recent fourth at 7f good — the Scorecard identifies this as the main danger and the trip and proximity to the pace both suit a horse that doesn't need to make up ground on testing surfaces.
runners_data.comment: Placed third and second in recent starts, Lushill has shown she can compete at this level and, with just 16 days between runs, arrives in good order carrying 125 lb from stall 10, her experience over today's trip an asset — though her inability to convert in her last six starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: The Kalonji Man

runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth in recent outings and a trainer hitting at just 4% in the past fortnight, The Kalonji Man makes little appeal here despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Grapple
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett juvenile who ran once, finishing 12th at 7f on good, and has been off 56 days; the yard's strong 14-day figures (9/47) keep the horse in the conversation but the long absence and sole form showing suggest this is a stepping-stone run rather than a winning mission, and the fade flag is noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked last on our figures, Grapple faces a stiff task at a 130 lb burden after 56 days off, though he has run over today's trip before and stall four offers a straightforward enough pitch.

races.paceDynamic: Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely competitive early gallop that is likely to be honest rather than suicidal but testing enough on Soft to Heavy ground over 7f at Salisbury. Both carry fade warnings, meaning the contested pace they generate is unlikely to be sustained into the final two furlongs, which will stretch the field considerably on this energy-sapping surface. Persian Land (midfield) and Lushill (prominent) are the prime beneficiaries of this shape — horses that can travel smoothly in the slipstream before picking off a tiring lead. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred berths; Hello You Ten from draw 2 and Our Fella from draw 6 are best placed to get early positions, while Minzaal Time from draw 5 faces a direct early duel — this race shape squarely favours hold-up and mid-to-late finishers who can exploit a flattening front rank on testing ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Midfield Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Minzaal Time and Hello You Ten fight for the lead and burn each other out by the 2f pole, leaving Persian Land to cruise through on the bridle.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a pressured, honest gallop that drains quickly on heavy ground, and Persian Land times a run from midfield to hit a flattening leader in the final furlong; the 7f trip and soft-going form (2W at similar conditions) make this the natural landing spot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Position Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early enough that one of the prominent types conserves energy and quickens clear from the front group before the closers engage.
scenarios.body: Lushill, with solid prominent form at 7f on similar going including a recent second, slots just off the pace and challenges decisively when the leaders crack; this suits a horse that has placed repeatedly at this trip without needing to lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners go too hard too soon and capitulate before the 3f pole, opening a window for a progressive or lightly-raced type to pounce from behind.
scenarios.body: Grapple (Ralph Beckett, Hector Crouch) or Oxber Flyer could exploit a truly collapsed pace as unknown quantities who haven't shown their ceiling; the scenario requires the front rank to self-destruct rather than merely tire, which is possible but not the most likely outcome on this pace evidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Hello You Ten or Minzaal Time blinks first in their duel and one settles into a controlled lead that proves just enough to outstay rivals on a day when closers can't fully accelerate through deep ground.
scenarios.body: Fade warnings on both make this the least likely outcome, but heavy ground can occasionally reward a horse that sets a moderate solo gallop once the duel resolves early; neither has the form profile to make this compelling.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hello You Ten or Minzaal Time breaks quickest — if Hello You Ten leads unchallenged from draw 2 while Minzaal Time is slow away, the single front-runner scenario could tip SCENARIO_D into the frame at the expense of the contested-pace thesis.

Persian Land's draw 8 means Callum Rodriguez must find a clean run through a mid-pack shuffle on heavy ground; any traffic trouble in the final quarter-mile would cost this horse the advantage the pace shape provides.
Lushill drawn widest (10) on a track where position in heavy going matters — William Cox will need to take a strong hold early to avoid wasting energy on the outside before the field compresses.

Grapple's 56-day absence and sole outing form (12th) make it a significant unknown; Hector Crouch and Ralph Beckett can produce fresh horses, so watch market moves closer to post time for any confidence signal.

The Kalonji Man's very low OR of 45 versus rivals rated up to 75 suggests it is here to fill the field rather than threaten, but it wears a hood and is out of its natural role — monitor whether it tracks up prominently early and compromises the expected pace shape.

runners_data.name: Soul Icon
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old prominent racer whose best sim-going form reads just 2 runs in 6 with no wins or places, and whose recent history at 21-24f GOO/SOF shows he has been competing at much longer trips — dropping back to 1m6f may sharpen him, but Josephine Gordon and Keiran Burke must produce a career-best on very testing ground.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Soul Icon steps into the unknown here, carrying 133 lb on a twentieth-day turnaround and giving punters precious little to go on — yet to score, but that lightly raced profile leaves plenty to work with.

runners_data.name: Quickthorn
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old front-runner for Hughie Morrison with one sim-going run (Soft, 16f) to his name here, giving him some relevant ground evidence; at OR 108 he is outrated by Amiloc and faces a pace duel he may not win, but if he settles into second gear he remains a staying threat.
runners_data.comment: Quickthorn won two starts back and returns here in good order after 21 days, with experience of both today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the fifth last time out is the one element rivals will point to.

runners_data.name: Lion's Pride
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's six-year-old hold-up horse returns after 133 days off with winning form over 12f on Good, now asked to tackle 1m6f on Soft-to-Heavy for the first time — the step up in trip is the critical unknown, and Robert Havlin will need to time his run precisely as the front-runners exhaust each other.
runners_data.comment: Lion's Pride landed a win in his last five starts and hails from a stable firing at 33% in the past fortnight, making him a genuine threat under 133 lb, though the 133-day absence is the key question mark against him.

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old leads on OR (114) among the front-running trio and has five sim-going runs, though none resulted in a win or place finish; Rossa Ryan is a major positive booking and Amiloc's 2/14f GOO effort shows some staying capacity, though his recent form string (4-66U7) raises reliability concerns.

runners_data.name: Nightime Dancer
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner (OR 93) and a confirmed front-runner for Richard Hannon, whose recent form (4-4070) and a history of finishing 7th-14th at 12-14f on Good suggests he will be outpaced and outclassed once the ground tests stamina at this marathon trip; wears a hood (b) which may sharpen early focus.
runners_data.comment: Nightime Dancer has run over today's trip and shaped with promise when fourth in two of his last five starts, while a 41-day break may have freshened him; the main concern is a trainer operating at just 4% in the last fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer — ensure this 1m6f Soft-to-Heavy Salisbury contest will be run at a strong, relentless gallop from the outset, with no horse able to dictate at a comfortable clip. Amiloc (highest OR at 114, Ralph Beckett, Rossa Ryan) is most likely to secure the lead, with Quickthorn pressing hard and Nightime Dancer completing a contested front rank that will drain stamina rapidly on this testing ground. The brutal pace battle among three leaders on heavy-ish ground sets up a race where the front rank burns each other off, creating a strong platform for those racing prominently in behind or stalking from slightly further back. This race shape most favours a horse with genuine stamina, the ability to race off a searching pace without expending early energy, and a finishing effort that has something left to call upon — a patient, prominent-to-midfield profile has the structural edge here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Stayer Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way front-runner battle burns through the leaders and a stayer picks up the pieces in the final quarter mile.
scenarios.body: Amiloc, Quickthorn, and Nightime Dancer fight a war of attrition through the heavy ground, leaving the winner to be the horse best able to sustain effort late; on this going, stamina rather than a sharp turn-of-foot decides it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Amiloc Controls, Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Amiloc settles into an unforced rhythm at the head of affairs and the other front-runners capitulate before the home turn.
scenarios.body: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old, ridden by Rossa Ryan, uses his superior OR of 114 to dictate a manageable pace that suits himself once the lesser front-runners fall away; his previous placed form over 14f on soft-adjacent ground gives him a stamina profile that can outlast them if the race is not truly brutal.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so searingly fast that it leaves a gap for Lion's Pride to thread through from the back on his return from 133 days off.
scenarios.body: Lion's Pride (John & Thady Gosden, Robert Havlin) drops out from his hold-up position as the front-runners implode, but he is stepping up markedly from his 12f winning form to 1m6f on Soft-to-Heavy ground, which introduces meaningful doubt about whether he stays and handles conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Nightime Dancer or one of the other front-runners capitulates early and the pace becomes unexpectedly moderate, producing a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: Without a true sustained gallop the race becomes a test of raw class and positional instinct rather than stamina, but with only five runners this is the least likely shape given the declared pace intentions of three confirmed leaders.

watchPoints.text: Amiloc (Rossa Ryan) and Quickthorn (Hector Crouch) are both committed front-runners — watch the first two furlongs to see who actually takes the lead and whether Nightime Dancer's presence forces an unsustainably fast pace that destroys the entire front rank.

Lion's Pride has not run for 133 days and is stepping from 12f Good wins to 1m6f Soft-to-Heavy — fitness on return and whether he truly stays the trip are the two variables that will determine whether his hold-up run materialises into a winning challenge.

Soul Icon's sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 2 runs) and recent form at extreme distances on Good ground raise the question of whether he has the class or condition to land a blow here — watch whether he tracks the pace prominently or gets detached.

Nightime Dancer's headgear (blinkers) may sharpen him early but his OR of 93 is a significant gap to the field — if he sets fractions too quickly before folding, he risks turning this into a true extreme stamina test that benefits whichever stayer survives the carnage.

runners_data.name: Gatlinburg
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature whose actual race position will be pushed into midfield because this field has too many confirmed runners who want to race prominently; 105 days off and a soft-going record of two runs with no wins or places (sim-going 2/5, 0W0P) does little to enhance a weak recent form string.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 105 days off, Gatlinburg faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip before and a rating of 70 offers a sliver of encouragement from stall two carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Letter
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner with the clearest back-of-the-field profile in the race, making her the chief beneficiary if the pace collapse scenario unfolds; Menuisier's yard is quiet (T14: 0/23) and just three runs to her name, but she has placed twice at 10f and holds soft-ground experience (1/3 sim-going, 0W0P).
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Scarlet Letter faces a stiff ask here, with a trainer who has drawn a blank in 24 outings over the past fortnight doing little to inspire confidence; experience over today's trip and going is the one genuine positive.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection: a front-runner with the most relevant profile for today — one win from three soft/similar-going appearances, a recent win at 9f on good ground, and Harry Davies booked for Portman's yard; the caveat is that all form has come on good ground with only three qualifying soft runs, so heavy is a slight extension of that evidence base.
runners_data.comment: Has raced over this trip before, and was runner-up two starts back, and a winner three starts back, but that eighth last time out is a concern; at 130 lb from stall 3, he arrives fit on a 15-day turnaround with our rating nudging above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Next Guilian
runners_data.note: Front-runner who steps up to 1m2f from a 1m base, with all four recorded turf runs on good ground; no soft-going form on record means today's conditions are an outright unknown and his claims rest entirely on upside over the trip, making him the most exposed of the pace setters.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Next Guilian faces a stiff ask here; a third five starts back offers a crumb of comfort, and he has experience of today's going, but the weight of 133 lb does little to help his cause.

runners_data.name: Eljowhary
runners_data.note: Prominent type with the highest OR in the race at 70 but a deeply discouraging form string (66400) and a fade-in-finish flag; all five recent runs have produced nothing on soft or standard ground, and the step to 1m2f looks more likely to expose the fade than cure it.
runners_data.comment: Eljowhary arrives here as our top-rated runner in the field, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions to draw on; yet to score in his last five starts, that winless streak is the chief concern he must overcome from stall five carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Sax Avoidance
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a clean, if short, progressive form profile (5-4-3) entirely on good-to-standard ground at 10f; Charlie Pike's yard is in modest form (T14: 1/9) and the jump to heavy going is unknown, but the step up to 1m2f in a pace-heavy race could see him stay on late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Sax Avoidance faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement heading into this on a handy 17-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Fanciulla Del West, Relentless Hero, Takeitorleaveit, and Next Guilian all carry genuine front-running tendencies into a 10-runner field, guaranteeing a contested gallop from the off on Soft To Heavy ground that will make stamina the defining currency. With four horses competing for the early lead over 1m2f in these conditions, the pace will be strong and sustained — likely fatal to those who fade in the finish, with Relentless Hero and Eljowhary both carrying that specific flag. The field holds more front-running types than can all secure their natural position; Takeitorleaveit, with the clearest tactical clarity and a recent win at similar distances, is best placed to dictate, while Next Guilian will press hard but lacks the heavy-ground form to sustain it. This race shape firmly favours a well-positioned prominent-to-lead runner with proven stamina and soft-ground resilience, able to control the tempo and grind rivals into the ground from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit secures the lead or a prominent position early and dictates a punishing, stamina-sapping gallop on the heavy ground.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace burns off the other pace horses, leaving Takeitorleaveit able to exploit its superior soft-ground record and grinding style through the final two furlongs; its 1W2P record in similar conditions and recent 15-day turnaround under Harry Davies with Jonathan Portman's yard in form supports this strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace War Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running quartet burn each other out setting a suicidal early gallop, leaving those held up or in midfield with energy to close.
scenarios.body: Miss Guinevere, carrying soft-going form (sim-going 1/4), and Scarlet Letter, a genuine hold-up type, would be able to pick up the pieces in the final furlong as the leaders empty; Sax Avoidance, who has shown progressive form over this type of trip, could also emerge from midfield.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Settles — One Leads
scenarios.trigger: If one pace horse breaks clear unchallenged early and the others drop in, reducing the gallop to a moderate tempo that suits a kicker.
scenarios.body: Fanciulla Del West, drawn 4 and freshest of the pace horses at 21 days off a solid form string, could slot into a rhythm if rivals defer, using its better recent form at 10f-12f to sustain a run; however, heavy ground is unexplored for most in this group, limiting confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the heavy going deteriorates further mid-race and turns it into an outright stamina slog that eliminates most of the field before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: In a truly brutal test, only the most stoic stayers with soft-ground pedigree survive, with Mid Flight — despite moderate recent form — and Scarlet River potentially finding a muddling finish to their liking at the expense of classier but faster-ground types; this is a low-probability scenario dependent on conditions worsening beyond current reporting.

watchPoints.text: Relentless Hero's fade-in-finish flag is critical: if he is still competitive turning for home he could collapse quickly and compromise Takeitorleaveit's chance by forcing an uneven pace in the early stages.

Next Guilian has zero soft-going form — if he pushes hard for the lead and capitulates before the final furlong, the resulting pace disruption could flatter horses further back in the field more than the form suggests they deserve.

Gatlinburg has been absent 105 days and is a genuine hold-up horse racing out of his natural position — monitor whether he settles in the middle of the pack or gets shuffled further back, as either outcome changes the closer scenario materially.

Eljowhary's trainer Eve Johnson Houghton holds the highest OR runner (70) in a heavy-ground field full of question marks — if conditions have not been as testing as reported and the ground rides better than expected, his class on paper becomes more relevant.

Takeitorleaveit's soft-going record (3 runs, 1W2P) is the best going-matching evidence in the race but is a small sample — watch market moves at the off to see whether connections are confident the heavy ground is within range of those performances.
